question: The AI Solution produced 13 Segment 120 requirements (12 bucketed SEG-120 + 1 mis-bucketed UNASSIGNED); the Test Solution has 8 Segment 120 rules (SEG120-R-001..SEG120-R-008). Does the Test Solution semantically cover all 13 AI requirements?

aiRequirementToTestRule.statement: The Print Data 2 Segment is only sent on Financial Transaction Response messages requiring large amounts of print data.
The Print Data 2 Segment always appears at the end of a Financial Transaction response.
The Print Data 2 Segment has a maximum length of 1,009 alphanumeric characters (01-1,009/a-z/A-Z).
There is a Field Separator between Field Nos. 1 and 2 and between Field Nos. 2 and 3 in the Print Data 2 Segment.
For Blackhawk phone activation and recharge, the Print Data field contains receipt text with a field delimiter '\' following each line of text sent to the device.
Segment Type field contains fixed value '120' for the Print Data 2 Segment.
Print Data 2 Segment (No. 120) Segment Length valid values are 001-1009.
In Print Data 2 Segment (Data Segment No. 120), field 1 (Segment Type) is required and must be present.
In Print Data 2 Segment (Data Segment No. 120), field 1 (Segment Type) must equal the fixed value 120.
In Print Data 2 Segment (Data Segment No. 120), field 2 (Segment Length) is required and must be present.
In Print Data 2 Segment (Data Segment No. 120), field 3 (Print Data) is required and must be present.
The Financial Transaction Response transaction includes Print Data 2 Segment (Data Segment No. 120).
The EMV Financial Transaction Response transaction includes Print Data 2 Segment (Data Segment No. 120).

note: This analysis measures whether the Test Solution rule catalog semantically covers every AI-generated requirement statement (100%). It is the inverse of segment-120-ai-coverage-report.json, which measures whether each Test Solution rule has adequate AI-generated test EVIDENCE (0% COVERED, 75% PARTIALLY_COVERED, 25% REVIEW_REQUIRED as of the 2026-09-23 P-01/P-02-WIDTH resolution). Both are needed: a rule can be semantically covered here while still lacking negative-test evidence there.
